reply_text:
Reviewed `receipt-lines` (`a6c40d4`) against `main`. **Two findings:**

1. **High — Printed amounts are 100× too large** — `receipt/render.py:2`  
   `format_money()` formats cents directly as dollars: `format_money(1299)` returns `$1299.00`, not `$12.99`. Two coffees at 450 cents print `$900.00` instead of `$9.00`. Convert cents to dollars before formatting. Add a literal expected-value assertion—the current test uses the same broken formatter to compute its expectation.

2. **Medium — The renderer never uses the new right-alignment helper** — `receipt/render.py:7`  
   `render_line()` still pads the name to 20 characters instead of using the 32-column `align()` function. Amounts with different digit counts end in different columns; the new layout test passes without exercising actual receipt rendering. Route rendered lines through `align()` and test their width/right edge with differently sized amounts.

All **3 tests pass**, but they miss both issues. No files changed. I’d fix these before merging.
